findings.issue: pkill -f patterns ('next') matched the agent's own bash command string, killing its own shell (exit 143) three times, including once destroying a test run at turn 78
findings.suggestion: Kill by port or PID (lsof -ti:3000 | xargs kill), or run pkill in a command whose text doesn't contain the pattern

findings.issue: Turbopack module-not-found for relative imports past the router dir was fixed by a jsconfig alias workaround without establishing the root cause and without consulting Next docs or the web (0 webSearches all session)
findings.suggestion: When a toolchain behaves inexplicably, check the Next.js docs/release notes before piling hypotheses; the alias is fine to keep, but the reasoning was guesswork

findings.issue: Two edit calls fired against text that didn't exist (attempting to 'fix' a file that was already correct)
findings.suggestion: Read or grep the file before editing when unsure of its exact contents

findings.issue: Background server start via (npm start &) died with the parent shell; ~5 turns spent on restart hygiene before using setsid</dev/null
findings.suggestion: Use setsid + nohup + redirect stdin from the start for long-lived dev servers

findings.issue: Considered the next-dev-loop skill (turn 55) but skipped it without reading it, then guessed agent-browser syntax and hit an unknown-command error
findings.suggestion: Read the available skill/help before choosing a verification workflow

summary: A disciplined session: 16 turns of reconnaissance, assumptions verified against real data, and a first full test run that passed 54/54 with zero fix cycles. Verification went well beyond the suite — screenshots compared to all 9 references at two viewports, HTTP probes, and a re-run after the final edit. The only weak spots were build-tool debugging by workaround (Turbopack imports) and sloppy process-kill hygiene that cost it a handful of turns.
